steps.title: Import Component, OnInit, OnDestroy, and Subscription from Angular core
steps.instruction: Import Component, OnInit, and OnDestroy from '@angular/core' and Subscription from 'rxjs'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary Angular lifecycle hooks and RxJS subscription management class.
steps.seedCode: // Import Component, OnInit, OnDestroy from '@angular/core' and Subscription from 'rxjs'
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary imports for Angular lifecycle hooks and RxJS subscription management are added to the file.
successCriteria: Component, OnInit, and OnDestroy are imported from '@angular/core', and Subscription is imported from 'rxjs'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the Angular lifecycle hooks and RxJS Subscription class needed for memory leak management.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some items, but check if you have all required imports: Component, OnInit, OnDestroy from '@angular/core' and Subscription from 'rxjs'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are incorrect or incomplete. You need to import Component, OnInit, OnDestroy from '@angular/core' and Subscription from 'rxjs'.

steps.title: Create the MemoryLeakHuntComponent class with Component decorator
steps.instruction: Create the MemoryLeakHuntComponent class with the @Component decorator, including selector and template metadata.
steps.hint: Use the imported Component decorator and define a class that implements OnInit and OnDestroy.
steps.expectedOutcome: A component class named MemoryLeakHuntComponent is created with proper Angular decorator and lifecycle interfaces.
successCriteria: MemoryLeakHuntComponent class exists with @Component decorator containing selector and template metadata, and implements OnInit and OnDestroy.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the component class with proper Angular structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your component has the @Component decorator with selector and template, and implements both OnInit and OnDestroy.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure is incomplete. Check that you have the @Component decorator with selector and template, and that the class implements OnInit and OnDestroy.

steps.title: Implement OnInit interface and define ngOnInit method
steps.instruction: In the MemoryLeakHuntComponent class, implement the OnInit interface and define an empty ngOnInit method.
steps.hint: Add 'implements OnInit' after the class name and create a public ngOnInit() method that returns void.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will implement the OnInit interface and have an empty ngOnInit method ready for initialization logic.
successCriteria: MemoryLeakHuntComponent implements OnInit and has a public ngOnInit method that returns void.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the OnInit interface and defined the ngOnInit lifecycle method. This prepares the component for initialization logic in the next steps.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've both implemented the OnInit interface (using 'implements OnInit') and defined the ngOnInit method with the correct signature (public, returns void).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't yet implement OnInit or have the ngOnInit method. Remember to add 'implements OnInit' after the class name and create a public ngOnInit(): void method.

steps.title: Implement OnDestroy interface and define ngOnDestroy method
steps.instruction: In your MemoryLeakHuntComponent class, implement the OnDestroy interface and create an empty ngOnDestroy method.
steps.hint: Add 'OnDestroy' to the class's 'implements' list and define a method named 'ngOnDestroy' with no return type annotation.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now implements both OnInit and OnDestroy interfaces, with empty lifecycle methods defined.
successCriteria: OnDestroy is added to the 'implements' list and an empty ngOnDestroy method is defined in the class.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've implemented the OnDestroy interface and defined the ngOnDestroy method. This is where we'll clean up subscriptions to prevent memory leaks.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added 'OnDestroy' to the 'implements' list and created a method named 'ngOnDestroy' with no parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should implement both OnInit and OnDestroy interfaces. Add 'OnDestroy' to the 'implements' list and define an empty 'ngOnDestroy' method.

steps.title: Add component state properties for timer and data
steps.instruction: Inside the MemoryLeakHuntComponent class, add two properties: a timer property of type number and a data property of type any[].
steps.hint: Declare these properties directly in the class body, above the ngOnInit method. Use TypeScript type annotations.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class will have timer and data properties declared, ready to be used for demonstrating potential memory leaks.
successCriteria: The MemoryLeakHuntComponent class contains a timer property of type number and a data property of type any[].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the timer and data properties. These will be used to simulate memory leak scenarios.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added one property, but need both timer (number) and data (any[]).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class doesn't have both required properties. Add timer: number and data: any[] inside the class.

steps.title: Declare a Subscription property for managing observables
steps.instruction: Inside the MemoryLeakHuntComponent class, declare a private property named 'dataSubscription' of type Subscription to manage observable subscriptions.
steps.hint: Add a property declaration with the correct type annotation and access modifier.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: declaring a subscription property
private userSubscription: Subscription;
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a properly typed Subscription property ready to store observable subscriptions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've declared a Subscription property that will help prevent memory leaks by properly managing observable subscriptions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the property is named 'dataSubscription', declared as private, and has the type 'Subscription'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Subscription property is missing or incorrect. Remember to declare a private property with the correct name and type.

steps.title: Create a simulated data stream in ngOnInit
steps.instruction: Inside the ngOnInit method, create an interval observable using RxJS's interval function that emits every second and updates the data property with the current count.
steps.hint: Use RxJS's interval function to create an observable that emits sequential numbers every 1000 milliseconds. Subscribe to it and update the data property with the emitted value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ngOnInit method will now contain an interval observable that updates the data property every second, simulating a data stream that needs cleanup.
successCriteria: An interval observable is created in ngOnInit that emits every 1000ms and updates the data property with the emitted value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a simulated data stream using RxJS interval. This observable will emit values every second, which we'll need to clean up later to prevent memory leaks.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using RxJS's interval function and subscribing to update the data property. Check that the interval emits every 1000ms.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interval observable wasn't properly created. Remember to import interval from 'rxjs', create an observable that emits every 1000ms, and subscribe to update the data property.

steps.title: Subscribe to the data stream and store the subscription
steps.instruction: Inside the ngOnInit method, subscribe to the interval observable and assign the returned subscription to the dataSubscription property.
steps.hint: Call the subscribe method on the interval observable and assign the result to this.dataSubscription.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: subscribing to an observable
const subscription = interval(1000).subscribe(value => console.log(value));
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now subscribes to the interval observable and stores the subscription reference for proper cleanup.
successCriteria: The interval observable is subscribed to and the subscription is assigned to the dataSubscription property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully subscribed to the observable and stored the subscription. This is essential for tracking observables that need cleanup.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're assigning the subscription to the dataSubscription property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The subscription wasn't properly stored. Remember to call subscribe() on the interval observable and assign the result to this.dataSubscription.

steps.title: Add cleanup logic in ngOnDestroy
steps.instruction: Inside the ngOnDestroy method, add logic to unsubscribe from the dataSubscription if it exists.
steps.hint: Check if the subscription property is defined before calling unsubscribe() on it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ngOnDestroy method now includes proper cleanup logic to prevent memory leaks by unsubscribing from the observable subscription.
successCriteria: ngOnDestroy contains an if statement that checks if dataSubscription exists and calls unsubscribe() on it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've implemented proper cleanup logic. This ensures that when the component is destroyed, the subscription is cleaned up to prevent memory leaks.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're checking if the subscription exists before calling unsubscribe().
steps.feedbackWrong: The cleanup logic is missing or incorrect. Remember to check if dataSubscription exists and call unsubscribe() on it.

steps.title: Add template structure to display data
steps.instruction: Update the component's template to include a header section and a paragraph that displays the timer value from your component state.
steps.hint: Access the timer property in your template using interpolation syntax {{ timer }}. Add a <h2> for the header.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will show a header and the current timer value, making the memory leak scenario visible in the UI.
successCriteria: Template contains an <h2> header and a paragraph displaying {{ timer }} using interpolation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the template structure to visualize the timer data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some template elements, but make sure you have both a header and the timer display using interpolation.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet show the header and timer display as requested. Check the interpolation syntax.

steps.title: Display the timer and data in the template
steps.instruction: Update the component's template to display the current timer value and data array length using interpolation.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to bind component properties in the template. You can display both the timer value and a message about data length.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show the timer value and data length when the component renders.
successCriteria: Template contains interpolation expressions for timer and data array length
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully bound component state to the template using interpolation.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using interpolation syntax {{ }} and displaying both timer and data length.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet display the timer and data. Remember to use interpolation with double curly braces.

steps.title: Add a button to manually trigger cleanup
steps.instruction: Add a button element to your component's template with a click handler that calls the ngOnDestroy method to manually test cleanup functionality.
steps.hint: Use the (click) event binding to call ngOnDestroy() when the button is clicked.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button (click)="ngOnDestroy()">Clean Up</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will include a button that, when clicked, triggers the ngOnDestroy method to simulate cleanup.
successCriteria: A button element with (click)="ngOnDestroy()" is added to the component's template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a button to manually test cleanup functionality. This allows you to verify that the ngOnDestroy logic works correctly.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added a button element with a click handler that calls ngOnDestroy().
steps.feedbackWrong: The button with click handler wasn't added correctly. Check that you've added a <button> element with (click)="ngOnDestroy()" in the template.
